key_claims: Training stress score of 100 points equals one hour at maximum power output; two hours at 50% intensity also equals 100 stress points
Fitness score is calculated by taking the last 42 training stress scores, adding them together and dividing by 42; sessions from 43 days ago no longer contribute
Acute training load (fatigue) is a running total of the last seven training stress scores
Over 90% of A1 athletes hit their seasonal goals through using performance management chart metrics
A cyclist took 2 minutes off a 10-minute climb segment after 8 weeks of structured training with a power meter, despite doing that segment 2-3 times weekly for years
specific_numbers: 100 training stress points = 1 hour full gas
42 training stress scores used for fitness calculation
7 training stress scores used for acute training load
2 minutes improvement on 10-minute climb after 8 weeks
cluster_reasoning: Episode focuses exclusively on power meter training methodology, performance management charts, training stress scores, and structured training metrics—core coaching pillar content about how to systematically improve cycling performance.
